doc.title: Jim Hall — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Playing with Coleman Hawkins and Hank Jones
summary: Sessions with Hawkins; Hank Jones on an out-of-tune piano.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Hmm. I think that people who aren’t musicians and people who… even maybe some musicians who don’t play a string instrument…
…wouldn’t ever think of such things—the overtones, the sound of the…
Yeah. I’m sure that Sonny Rollins thinks of that, you know. And I imagine Coleman Hawkins did, as well. (laughs) I actually played with Coleman Hawkins a couple times, just kind of jam sessions but…
He was great. I was, you know, a huge fan. I just… but I can’t… Oh, yeah. There was… somebody threw together a bunch of musicians for some kinda something

on Long Island. There were some really good players. Coleman Hawkins… Hank Jones played piano. That was funny ‘cause the piano was terribly out of tune. And Hank was such a marvelous… He, somehow when he… by the time he finished, it sounded like it was in tune. He just would choose notes that worked.
That was, that was a great experience.
